concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset.note: He loved the simple worship of ordinary, upright people — saying many techinnot and bakkashot from the large siddurim, as is the way of the kosher common folk.
He admonished repeatedly to sing zemirot on Shabbat and Motzaei Shabbat. He himself sang many zemirot every Shabbat before his final illness.
The core principle: 'the essence of Judaism is in complete simplicity and wholeheartedness, without any sophistication.'
He was angry at those who consider themselves too wise/sophisticated for simple worship — this is the negative counterpoint to peshitut.
